name: YouthLine
summary: Teen-to-teen crisis support line where young people help other young people.

sections.title: About YouthLine
sections.text: YouthLine is a teen-to-teen crisis support service where young people help other young people navigate difficult times. Operated by Lines for Life, YouthLine is staffed by trained teen volunteers who provide peer support, crisis intervention, and referrals to youth ages 11-21. The unique peer-to-peer model recognizes that young people often prefer talking to someone their own age who understands their experiences, making YouthLine an accessible entry point for youth seeking help.

sections.title: Who Can Contact YouthLine
sections.text: YouthLine serves young people ages 11-21 who are struggling with any issue—you don't have to be in crisis to reach out. Common reasons youth contact YouthLine include stress, anxiety, depression, relationship problems, family conflict, bullying, identity questions, grief, suicidal thoughts, and simply needing someone to talk to. If you're a young person who needs support but isn't sure where to turn, YouthLine's peer counselors are here to listen without judgment.

sections.title: How to Reach YouthLine
sections.text: Call 1-877-968-8491 to talk with a teen peer counselor. Teen volunteers answer calls from 4 PM to 10 PM Pacific Time, Monday through Friday, and 6 PM to 10 PM Pacific Time on weekends. Outside these hours, trained adult volunteers provide support. You can also text teen2teen to 839863, chat online at oregonyouthline.org, or email help@oregonyouthline.org. All services are free and confidential.

sections.title: Teen Volunteer Counselors
sections.text: YouthLine's teen helpers are high school students who complete an extensive training program covering crisis intervention, active listening, mental health awareness, and suicide prevention. Teen volunteers bring lived experience of adolescent challenges while receiving professional supervision and support. The peer model reduces barriers to seeking help—many young people find it easier to open up to someone their own age who can genuinely relate to their experiences with school, relationships, and growing up.

sections.title: Beyond the Line
sections.text: YouthLine offers more than crisis support. The website provides self-help resources, information about mental health, and tips for supporting friends in crisis. YouthLine also runs school-based programs that train students in peer support and suicide prevention. If you're a young person interested in helping others, YouthLine offers volunteer opportunities for teens who want to make a difference in their community by supporting their peers.
